summary.text: Josh Turek is the Democratic nominee. A Council Bluffs native and four-time Paralympian on the U.S. national basketball team, he worked for a mobility-equipment company before winning a state House seat in 2022 by six votes. He is running for the open seat of retiring Sen. Joni Ernst (R), emphasizing health care, public education and costs for middle-class families.

paragraphs.text: Turek grew up in Council Bluffs, Iowa, and was born with spina bifida; his campaign website links the condition to his father's exposure to Agent Orange in Vietnam and says he had 21 surgeries by the age of 12.

He graduated from Abraham Lincoln High School in Council Bluffs and played basketball at Southwest Minnesota State University, graduating in 2002 with a bachelor's degree, and he later earned an MBA from DeVry University.

Before seeking office he was a professional basketball player and played for the U.S. national team in four Paralympic Games, medaling in three; his campaign website calls him a two-time Paralympic gold medalist and says his basketball career ended with a gold medal in Tokyo in 2021.

While playing professionally, Turek began as volunteer director of the Ryan Martin Foundation, which gives disabled children opportunities to play sports for free; he also worked with patients and doctors at a wheelchair and mobility-assistance company to provide mobility devices and complex rehabilitation technology, according to his campaign website.
He was inducted into the athletic halls of fame at Abraham Lincoln High School and Southwest Minnesota State University and into the National Wheelchair Basketball Association Hall of Fame.
Turek won Iowa House District 20 in 2022, defeating Republican Sarah Abdouch by 3,403 votes to 3,397, and was re-elected in 2024 with 52.5% of the vote over James Wassell.
His campaign website says the seat had voted for Donald Trump twice before his first win.
Ballotpedia lists his 2025-2026 House committee assignments as Human Resources, Natural Resources, State Government and Veterans Affairs, plus the Health Policy Oversight Committee.
He won the June 2, 2026, Democratic primary for U.S. Senate over Zach Wahls, 62.6% to 37.3%.
Turek lives in Council Bluffs with his wife, Jarolin, who works in health care.
